brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Color-coded category clusters with subtle glow create immediate topic legibility against the dark canvas
Spatial metaphor genuinely embodies the brief — clusters float with proximity hinting at semantic relation
File row typography is consistent: name plus muted format chip and size reads cleanly at scan speed
dominant_weaknesses: Cluster placement feels arbitrary rather than meaningful — overlaps occlude content (Product Strategy, Marketing Assets) without spatial logic
Connection lines between clusters are nearly invisible, undermining the entire 'proximity = relation' premise of the canvas
Toolbar, search, and minimap feel like generic chrome bolted on; no visual language ties them to the spatial system
fix_priorities: Resolve z-order and collision: clusters must not occlude each other's content; introduce intentional spacing or smart stacking
Strengthen relational edges — visible weighted lines or gravity fields so proximity actually communicates topic relationships
Unify chrome with canvas: minimap should mirror real cluster colors/positions, toolbar should adopt the same translucent card language
Add a hierarchy cue (cluster size or density reflecting file count/importance) so the canvas rewards zoom and exploration
rationale.norman_balance: Decent visceral pull from glowing clusters, but behavioral clarity suffers from occlusion and weak relational signals, leaving reflective payoff merely conceptual.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the spatial cluster metaphor is present, but without visible relations or collision logic it reads as scattered cards rather than a true proximity-driven canvas.
